issues.observed: Months are displayed in a non-chronological sequence such as April, August, December, February, January and July. Connecting these points creates a false time-series path.
issues.desired: All trend visuals should follow fiscal or calendar chronology, with the chosen convention clearly stated.
issues.action: Create a numeric MonthSort or FiscalMonthNumber column, set MonthName to Sort by column, and use a YearMonth key when the axis spans multiple years. Validate that both trend charts use the same chronological order.

issues.observed: Revenue and YoY growth are plotted against a common monetary scale. The red growth series is compressed against zero and is effectively unreadable in both performance visuals.
issues.desired: Revenue and percentage growth must have distinct, clearly labelled scales or be separated into aligned visuals.
issues.action: For Regional Performance, use a native line and clustered column chart with revenue on the primary axis and YoY growth on a secondary percentage axis. For the horizontal category view, use aligned revenue bars plus a separate growth dot or variance panel, or use a compact matrix with revenue and conditional-format growth.

issues.observed: Each slicer exposes only one unchecked list item and a scrollbar. The visible items suggest FY 2022, London and Beauty, while the charts still contain multiple years, regions and categories, making active filter context ambiguous.
issues.desired: Executives should immediately understand whether the page is filtered and what period, region and category are active.
issues.action: Replace the list slicers with compact dropdown slicers showing All or the selected value. Add a date or fiscal-period range control, a visible Reset filters button, and a dynamic subtitle summarising the current filter context. Verify slicer interactions with every visual.

issues.observed: A prominent trial-capacity warning occupies the top of the deployed experience.
issues.desired: A board-facing report should open in a licensed, production-branded environment without trial or capacity warnings.
issues.action: Deploy the report to an appropriately licensed production workspace or embedded capacity and remove the trial-state banner before executive distribution.

issues.observed: The page begins directly with slicers and contains no visible Executive Overview title, reporting-period summary, last-refresh timestamp or concise business context.
issues.desired: The page should establish its purpose and current reporting context before presenting metrics.
issues.action: Add a restrained page header containing Executive Overview, a dynamic period/filter subtitle and last refreshed date. Keep it compact so it does not materially reduce chart space.

issues.observed: Field and measure names such as TotalRevenue, GrossMarainPct, YoYGrowthPct, RegionName and CategoryName are exposed directly. GrossMarainPct also appears misspelled.
issues.desired: Board-facing labels should use concise business language such as Total Revenue, Gross Margin %, YoY Growth, Region and Category.
issues.action: Rename fields for this visual or apply display folders and presentation-friendly measure names. Replace auto-generated titles with intentional titles and correct the GrossMarainPct spelling without changing the underlying measure logic.

issues.observed: The cards show current values only. There are no prior-period comparisons, targets, directional indicators or threshold explanations, so 109.6% growth and 14 risk areas lack decision context.
issues.desired: Each KPI should indicate direction and materiality against an appropriate prior period or target, especially the risk metric.
issues.action: Use the Power BI new Card visual or a compact companion label to show prior-year variance, target variance and status colour. Define what constitutes a Risk Area in a tooltip or info panel. Do not add comparison values unless supported by validated measures.

issues.observed: YoY Growth is displayed as 109.6%, an unusually large result that could mean either 109.6% growth or a 109.6 index/ratio. The page provides no definition.
issues.desired: The displayed percentage should have an unambiguous, validated business definition.
issues.action: Validate the DAX measure and formatting with finance. Confirm whether the intended result is percent change, a current/prior ratio or an index. Preserve the measure if correct, but add a definition tooltip and appropriate sign or wording.

issues.observed: Green and red are used as series identifiers for years and measures, even when they do not represent positive and negative status. This conflicts with common executive status semantics and is weak for colour-vision accessibility.
issues.desired: Neutral categorical colours should identify series, while green and red should be reserved for validated favourable and adverse status.
issues.action: Use a consistent primary blue for revenue, a secondary neutral or teal for comparison series, and reserve red for adverse exceptions. Add markers, labels or line styles so meaning does not depend on colour alone.

issues.observed: Separate year-coloured lines are connected across a month axis, but the unordered categories make seasonal comparison and recent trajectory difficult to interpret.
issues.desired: The charts should clearly support either continuous time analysis or like-for-like seasonal comparison.
issues.action: Choose one analytical mode: use a continuous YearMonth axis for trajectory, or use correctly ordered fiscal months with separate current-year and prior-year lines for seasonal comparison. Emphasise the current period and de-emphasise the comparator.

issues.observed: Only London and Scotland appear, while the page gives no explanation of whether this is the complete regional scope or the result of filtering.
issues.desired: The chart and page context should make geographic coverage explicit.
issues.action: Verify the region dimension and slicer state. If only two regions are valid, retitle the chart or subtitle it accordingly. If additional regions are being excluded, expose the active filter and correct slicer interactions.

issues.observed: KPI values are readable but sit in flat white blocks with substantial unused space and limited differentiation between standard metrics and the risk metric.
issues.desired: The KPI row should be the strongest visual tier, with consistent labels, values, comparison context and restrained status emphasis.
issues.action: Increase card value weight, reduce unused vertical padding, apply subtle borders or shadows consistently, and use a controlled warning treatment for Risk Areas only when thresholds justify it.

issues.observed: Axis and legend text is small, chart titles are verbose, and the category chart lacks useful revenue labels. The regional chart also leaves large plot areas without decision-relevant annotations.
issues.desired: Charts should be readable at executive presentation distance and expose the values needed for quick comparison.
issues.action: Increase axis and legend text modestly, shorten titles, apply consistent currency display units, add selective end or data labels, and remove redundant legends when series meaning is already clear from titles or direct labels.

issues.observed: The grid is generally aligned, but the page relies on default Power BI styling, faint section separation and inconsistent visual proportions.
issues.desired: A premium executive page should feel intentionally composed while remaining restrained and native to Power BI.
issues.action: Apply a documented spacing grid, consistent visual padding, subtle section containers and a cohesive report theme. Preserve the current two-row analytical structure rather than adding decorative elements.

summary: The deployed page contains all required KPI and analytical areas and has a workable basic grid, but it is not yet suitable for CEO/CFO use. The critical analytical defect is the non-chronological month ordering, which makes both trend lines misleading. Revenue and percentage growth also share incompatible scales, rendering the growth series unreadable. Ambiguous slicer state, technical field names, absent page context and the production trial banner further reduce executive trust. Most improvements are achievable with native Power BI formatting, sorting, slicer, card and combo-chart capabilities without changing measure semantics.
reference_rejected_ideas: The exact Power BI application chrome, branded left navigation and toolbar shown in the reference are host or embedding-shell concerns, not necessary report-canvas content.

A horizontal revenue bar chart with independently positioned YoY dots on a secondary percentage axis is not a standard native Power BI combo visual; aligned native visuals or a matrix are more maintainable alternatives.

Tiny sparklines inside every KPI card are optional and may require the new Card visual, layered visuals or a custom visual. Prior-period and target context is analytically more important than matching this decoration.
The reference's specific Jan 1 to Apr 30 date range and global region/category values should not be copied unless they match the actual fiscal calendar and validated data scope.
The reference's dense sidebar navigation would consume report canvas space if reproduced inside Power BI; native page navigation or an external app shell is preferable.
